Goma and Bukavu, the provincial capitals of North and South Kivu, fell to the AFC/M23 and the RDF in January and February 2025 (the US Treasury counts thousands of civilians killed in Goma); the state cannot tax, administer or police them, and the rebels went on to take Kavumu airport and, in December 2025, Uvira on the Burundian border, from which they withdrew by February 2026. constraints.text: The 2028 succession and the constitution. The current constitution bars a third term and ends Tshisekedi's mandate at the close of 2028. The court's clearance of a referendum route (July 2026) is contested: the Catholic bishops' conference (CENCO) said on 20 June 2026 that a 'forced passage' risked the balkanisation of the country, the C64 opposition bloc called the move 'high treason', and the ruling Sacred Union of the Nation answered that a few bishops cannot substitute themselves for the institutions. Any Kinshasa deal with Kigali or the M23 is read in that light.

paradoxes.text: The more Kinshasa negotiates the peace, the less it controls the state that would keep it. The Washington and Doha tracks require an inclusive national dialogue and internal reform, yet the constitutional route to a third term turns the opposition and the bishops against the presidency just as the eastern front needs unity. A deal signed in Doha or Washington is only as strong as the Kinshasa politics that implement it.

grand_strategy.reading: Kinshasa has lost its two largest eastern cities to a rebellion that its neighbour backs, and it cannot retake them alone, so it has spent 2025-2026 buying partners: Burundian troops in South Kivu, Ugandan operations against the ADF, Qatar's Doha track, Washington's minerals-for-security deal and an Angolan mediation that has come and gone. Every track gives it a seat and gives its enemies one too, which is why the strategy works by keeping the initiative with others rather than by winning on the ground. The minerals are the currency of the whole effort and the reason the outside powers are present, with China already holding most of the cobalt through Sicomines and the United States now seeking access. The 2028 succession has moved the decisive contest from the eastern front to the capital, where the Catholic bishops and the opposition are the only national forces able to stop a third term, and that is the constraint no foreign mediator can remove.

stances.note: Rival, not adversary, read from Kinshasa's side. For adversary: the RDF fights inside the DRC alongside AFC/M23 (UN experts: 3,000-4,000 troops in 2024), took Goma and Bukavu in January-February 2025 with the rebels, the US sanctioned Minister Kabarebe (20 Feb 2025) and the RDF (2 Mar 2026), and the Congolese government calls Rwanda's presence an invasion. Against: Kinshasa's declared aim is the Rwandan withdrawal and the Washington framework, not the end of the Rwandan state; it signed the Washington framework (27 Jun 2025) and the Accords (4 Dec 2025) with Kigali, and its ceasefire complaints go to the Washington mechanism, not to a war aim. The same reading the RWA card gives from the other side, with the same sources. Bond grievance: the wars of 1996-2003 and the 1994 refugee camps. State of play, 14 Oct 2026: the US asked Rwanda to withdraw and end its M23 support.

stances.note: Adversary in the mortal sense, read from Kinshasa's side, and the only adversary in this file. The test of the ontology is met on both sides: the AFC's political leadership openly aims to topple the government in Kinshasa (its president Corneille Nangaa: 'our objective is neither Goma nor Bukavu but Kinshasa'), and Kinshasa's court sentenced Nangaa to death in absentia in August 2025 (Crisis Group). The government's aim is the rebels' defeat and disarmament, not a settlement that keeps them. Trend stable: the Doha roadmap of August 2026 has not ended the fighting.
